rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because threads in a warp share instruction execution, and their memory requests can be combined. Similar control flow avoids divergent paths that leave some threads inactive. Accessing consecutive, properly aligned memory lets the GPU serve the warp with fewer memory transactions, improving throughput.

rows.name: spoken-why-during-coding-frozen-21
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: A circular array lets push and pop run in constant time without shifting elements or allocating memory. Tracking the head and current size makes all 17 slots usable, rejects pushes when full, and detects empty pops. Advancing indices modulo 17 preserves FIFO order when they wrap around.
